newsitem.title: USA: Substance Abuse saliva test launch delayed.
newsitem.headline: Substance Abuse saliva test launch delayed.

text.p: Substance Abuse Technologies Inc said on Monday that a consultant's preliminary report projected that August 1999 would be the earliest launch date for its saliva-based drug and alcohol testing product.
The company previously announced December 1998 as the product launch date.

In addition, the consulting firm, Owen & Associates Inc, said the total additional costs of the project will come to roughly $18.4 million, not $10 million to $12 million as previously announced by Substance Abuse, the company said.
As a result of the delay and added expenditure, Substance Abuse said its board of directors was reviewing how the product's testing could be funded.

The company added that it had not authorized a spinoff of U.S. Drug Testing Inc, which is 75.4 percent owned by Substance Abuse. Substance Abuse said it was making the statement in response to speculation. "A successful U.S. Drug Testing device could bring benefits to Substance Abuse that argue against a spinoff," the company said.

However, it added that if U.S. Drug were privately owned, an investment by a venture capital investor or group of venture capital investors could result in reducing Substance Aubse's ownership to less than 50 percent.
"Until now, because of the product potential and the significant dilution which would occur from such a financing, Sustance Abuse's board has opposed this approach," Substance Abuse said.
Substance Abuse also reported that its board had authorized the purchase of an additional two million shares of U.S. Drug's common stock for $2.5 million.
